I wanted Grok Bot to set my Tesla navigation based on my schedule. There's still no official Tesla app connection. Guess what? I figured it out again 😉 Grok Bot can now get my Tesla navigation ready.

Here's the workflow:

I asked Grok Bot to book a dentist appointment. It texted the office from my Mac. 7 minutes later, the confirmation came in. Grok Bot read the text and added the event to my calendar with the address and time.

Got in my Cybertruck and the appointment was already on the map. Tapped "Start Driving" and drove. Grok Bot handled everything, A to Z.

How to set it up:

1. Grok Bot: Turn on phone calendar write access.
2. Tesla app: Profile → Settings → turn on Calendar Sync.
3. iPhone: Settings → Tesla → Calendars → Full Access.

The key is to always have Grok Bot include the address and time in the event. That's how your car picks up the destination instantly.

I gave a talk at a Claude Community House titled "How to Make Claude Multiplayer with Notion"

I feel that AI made us 10x more productive individually... and worse together. 

We became meatbag APIs™

Meaning my agent writes something, I paste it to you, you paste it to yours, and so on and so forth. 

It’s cause every person's context lives in their own AI chat. Your agent can't see what mine knows. The fix is a shared context layer in Notion. 

Own the context in Notion, rent the compute from Claude, Grok Bot, your own harness etc.  

Core context layer includes tasks, docs, meetings, decisions, projects and skills. Once those live in one place, every teammate's agent reads the same context layer.  Begone copy-pasta-agent relay!

note_tweet.text:
I thought I knew where my money goes. Then Grok Bot read 12 months of my bank statements and I had to sit down.

I didn't do anything fancy. I exported a year of statements and let Grok Bot go through them. 1,904 transactions. In the video you can see the statement tape flying by while it tags everything: food, transport, rent, fun, and the ones I really didn't want to see: duplicate, unused 4 months, price up 30%, fee.

The donut on the right builds up as it goes. $3,941 a month, 38% housing, 19% food, 14% fun. Nothing crazy there. The problem was hiding in the small stuff.

Look at the subscriptions wall. 12 tiles, each with the price and when I last used it. Then the stamps start landing:

Cinewave, last used 4 months ago: CANCEL
FitPulse, 6 months ago: CANCEL
PhotoPro, 7 months ago: CANCEL
LangBuddy, 5 months ago: CANCEL
MealKit+, 3 months ago, $59.99: CANCEL
GymCo charged twice, a literal duplicate: CANCEL

The stuff I actually use, the music app, cloud storage, VPN, notes, got a green KEEP. 7 cancelled, $172.95 a month back.

Then it went after the bills. It drafted emails to my internet provider, phone plan and car insurance, waited for replies and countered:

internet $79 → $55
phone $45 → $30
insurance $142 → $119

Total: $2,819 a year saved, and my projected spend for next year is down 17%.

My honest opinion:

Nobody overspends on purpose. We overspend through things we said yes to once and forgot. A free trial that turned paid. A gym that charged twice. A price that went up 22% and nobody noticed because it's on autopay. It's never one big mistake, it's thirty tiny leaks.

And this is the kind of job where an AI agent is actually useful in real life. Reading 1,904 transactions is boring. Calling your provider to negotiate is awkward. A bot doesn't get bored and doesn't feel awkward.

The part I liked most: it never cancelled anything on its own judgment alone. It looked at real usage. If I opened an app yesterday, it stayed. That's the difference between a smart audit and a bot that just cuts everything to make the number look big.

Comment "AUDIT" and I'll DM you how I set it up: how to export your statements, the rules it uses to flag subscriptions, and the email it sends to negotiate bills

And be honest in the replies: how many subscriptions are you paying for right now that you haven't opened this month? I had 7, and I would have sworn it was 2
